state:
**Goal `limit-handler-reach`, Stage 2 is on disk: a memory breach inside `Core\Arr::from`'s drain runs the program's `Core\Fatal::onLimit` handler.** Stage 3 is untouched. Goal `the-description-is-owed`'s whole list is this goal's Stage 1 floor.

What Stage 2 turned out to be, and `crates/nvs-runtime/src/sequence.rs`'s module doc § *What it costs, and what bounds it* is its home: the breach was never raised by `crate::abi::affordable`. The drain asked for one element in front of a push whose `Vec` doubling took the request past its whole budget, reserve included; the entry poll of the next driven `advance` (`nvs_safepoint`) found it and did call the handler, which was stopped at its first member call. `drain` now prices the growth, so the refusal happens in front of it and `run_helper`'s failure arm runs the handler on an intact reserve. No edit to `crates/nvs-runtime/src/abi.rs` or `crates/nvs-runtime/src/ctx/hooks.rs` was needed.

Stage 0's catch-up is done with it: the module doc paragraph that stated the bug is gone.

The pack was missing `crates/nvs-runtime/src/ctx/limits.rs` and `crates/nvs-runtime/src/ctx/safepoint.rs` from `context.modules`; both are added, with `crates/nvs-host/src/watchdog.rs` and `crates/nvs-host/src/isolate.rs` for Stage 3.

items.text: **Find what the watchdog charges a request against after `Core\Config::set('limits.cpu_time', …)`** — `crates/nvs-runtime/src/ctx/limits.rs:427` is `refresh_limits`, which moves `Ctx::cpu_limit`; `crates/nvs-host/src/isolate.rs:653` is the one `watch.publish` at request start; `crates/nvs-host/src/watchdog.rs:577` is `publish` and `crates/nvs-host/src/watchdog.rs:205` builds the record that carries the baseline. None of the three was read by the session that wrote this, so the anchors are pointers and not findings. Say how a narrowed ceiling can reach the published record, and what a request that started under no cap has published.

**Make the narrowed ceiling the one the sweep charges, keeping the charge's starting point** — `crates/nvs-host/src/watchdog.rs:232` is `baseline`; the goal's Stage 3 prose forbids a republish that takes a new one, and a child's narrowing must not move the root's.

**Pin it** — `tests/conformance/error/a-cpu-time-narrowed-by-config-set-stops-a-loop-that-calls-nothing.nvst`, the case the Stage 3 check names: an `onLimit` handler, a `set` to a short `cpu_time` and a loop that calls nothing. `tests/conformance/error/a-loop-that-allocates-nothing-is-stopped-by-the-cpu-ceiling.nvst:1` is the sibling whose shape it takes.

backlog: A member whose own allocation is not priced in front of it can still overshoot the whole budget and enter the handler with no reserve; `crates/nvs-runtime/src/sequence.rs`'s module doc says why the growth is what has to be priced, and `crate::abi::affordable` is the seam a member found with that shape uses.

`bun nv playbook --retire` drops the playbook bullet that names goal `limit-handler-reach`'s Stage 3 as the fix once the case is green: `docs/agent/playbook/writing-a-test-case/an-example-or-attack-that-ends-on-the-cpu-limit-cannot.md`.
When this goal's last check goes green the driver takes goal `plain-comments`.
